observations: WHICH PHONE, AND A CONFLICT THAT MUST BE READ BEFORE THE REST OF THIS RECORD. `.cursor/rules/device-testing.mdc` carries a table naming `RF8Y703DR2D` (SM-A165F, Galaxy A16) as the test target and listing `R58MB3SGZVL` (SM-A405FM, Galaxy A40) as 'off limits to every agent', on the ground that the A40 is the owner's own phone. On 2026-10-03 the owner overrode that directly and repeatedly in the session that produced this record: 'твой телефон, который ты управляешь, это Samsung Galaxy A40. Именно с ним ты и работаешь.' The owner's live instruction was taken as authoritative, so this run was driven on the A40 - a device the rule file still calls forbidden. The rule and the owner's instruction now disagree and one of them is stale; reconciling them is a human act, because no program reads this paragraph. The readings are the A40's own: `getprop ro.product.model` reads `SM-A405FM`, `ro.build.version.sdk` reads `30` (Android 11), `wm size` reads `1080x2340`, `wm density` reads `Physical density: 480` - 30 dpi denser than the A16 the rule names, so no coordinate in this record may be reused on that device.

WHICH READINGS BELONG TO WHICH BUILD, stated first because two consecutive revisions were driven. The digest this record names is 2a62d6e59b1280f1d18be91cd253e91d416de0d267df0c81cbcca8f6ea570936, which `releaseSourceDigest('apps/2026-10-01-lawn-round-log')` returns over 152 files. Observations 6, 7 and 8 (the customer-order fix, the CSV export and share handoffs, and the release artifact install) were taken on this revision's build. Observations 4, 5, 9, 10, 11 were taken on the immediately preceding build of the same series, digest 1e61743bfb1794f8034c5553f809bafdffef7c62d1e7b40655b4410493043197, which differs from this one by exactly two changes - the customer-editor fix below and one `iconGlyph` value in `store/listing.json` - neither of which touches the payment path, the appearance preference, the due-day list, the empty-state copy or the round data on disk. They are carried here rather than re-driven because re-running an unchanged path would produce a second reading of the same behaviour rather than new evidence, and the honest limit is stated instead of hidden: they are readings of a build one revision behind, named by digest.

The install, and the defect this revision fixed to make it possible. On the previous revision, installing the debug artifact on the A40 failed with `INSTALL_FAILED_CONFLICTING_PROVIDER: ... provider name com.gexetr.lawnroundlog.fileprovider (in package com.gexetr.lawnroundlog.debug) is already used by com.gexetr.lawnroundlog`, because the FileProvider authority was a literal naming the release applicationId and the debug variant therefore claimed a provider the installed release package owned. After the authority was derived (`android:authorities="${applicationId}.fileprovider"` in AndroidManifest.xml, `fileProviderAuthority(context)` in ui/history/HistoryViewModel.kt), `adb -s R58MB3SGZVL install -r app-debug.apk` reports `Success` and `pm list packages` lists both `com.gexetr.lawnroundlog` and `com.gexetr.lawnroundlog.debug` side by side. Both packages are now installed on this phone, which is the state the fix exists to allow.

Defect C, the 'Due today' tab (read on digest 1e61743bfb17). Two customers were added through the app's own New-customer screen; both were due, so the tab listed both. Marking Alice at the `Mark Alice as mowed` target moved `Total owed` to `$40.00` and dropped her out, leaving `Bob`. Marking Bob moved `Total owed` to `$80.00` and left the tab empty, where it then rendered `Nobody left today` and `Every customer on today's round has been recorded. Open Whole round to see the rest, or push the day if the weather turns.` Before this revision the same state rendered the first-run `No customers yet` copy over a round of two recorded customers, because the day list fell back to the whole ordered round whenever nothing was due - so the tab listed people who were demonstrably not due today.

Defect A, the payment edit (read on digest 1e61743bfb17), driven through the UI because it is the defect that corrupted a ledger. In Alice's record, a `10` in the `Amount received` field and `Record payment` produced a payment row reading `$10.00` / `2026-10-03`, and `History` then read `3 entries`. `Edit the entry for Alice` on that payment row opened a dialog titled `Correct the entry`; the amount was changed to `25` and saved, after which the ledger still read `3 entries` and the row read `$25.00`. That is the fix: the edit used to call `recordPayment`, which writes a payment dated today, while `Round.setPayment` looks the record up by `customerId` AND `dateIso`, so correcting an earlier payment appended a second one and left the original - moving the balance by the sum instead of the difference. The correction now goes through `RoundViewModel.restatePayment`, which keeps the payment's own `dateIso`.

The customer-order defect, found by an independent evaluation of the previous revision and fixed in this one, then measured on this build. `CustomerViewModel.validatedCustomer()` rebuilt the record from the six fields the form shows, and `RoundViewModel.upsertCustomer` replaces a stored row with the handed-over `Customer` verbatim; because `Round.ordered` sorts by `position`, then `createdAt`, then `id`, an operator who corrected anything about an existing customer silently reset both sort keys to zero and moved that customer to the head of the round. On the A40 with the round reading `1 Alice / 2 Bob`, `Open Bob` was tapped, `7 Oak Ave` was typed into the Address field and `Save` was tapped; the round afterwards still read `1 Alice / 2 Bob`, and `Bob`'s row is at the same y-coordinate as before. The fix carries `position`, `createdAt` and `active` through the draft, and `CustomerViewModelTest.correctingACustomerKeepsHisPlaceInTheRound` fails when the reset is reintroduced - measured by reverting the two fields and reading `FAIL testDebugUnitTest - 35 tests completed, 1 failed`, then restoring them and reading `PASS - 35 tests, 0 failures`.

The CSV handoffs, driven on this revision in the owned state, because they are the connective claim the slot's job coverage rests on (`differentiators.json`, `data_out`). The debug package was relaunched after `am force-stop` with `--ez com.gexetr.lawnroundlog.DEBUG_UNLOCK true`, a hook guarded by `BuildConfig.DEBUG` that a release build constant-folds away, and the bottom bar's label then read `Unlocked`. History's header exposed two 48 dp actions whose accessible names were read from the hierarchy, never guessed: `Export CSV` at `840,182` and `Share CSV` at `984,182`. Tapping `Export CSV` opened `com.google.android.documentsui/com.android.documentsui.picker.PickActivity` - the `ActivityResultContracts.CreateDocument("text/csv")` handoff reaching the platform - listing the existing `lawn-round-log.csv` (358 B, Oct 2) that an earlier run left in Downloads; I cancelled with back rather than overwrite it, so this record does not claim a write. Tapping `Share CSV` opened `android/com.android.internal.app.ChooserActivity` showing `lawn-round-log.csv` as the item on offer, with Telegram, VK, Quick Share and Link Sharing as targets, which is the `Intent.ACTION_SEND` path and, more usefully, proof that the FileProvider Uri the app hands out is readable by other packages under the derived authority. Back dismissed the chooser and the app resumed on History, which is the surface it left from.

The appearance preference (read on digest 1e61743bfb17), measured as a number and across a process death rather than by eye. Choosing `Light` on a phone whose system is in dark mode repainted the app to `mean_luminance=237.6` with centre pixel `(246,244,228)`; after `am force-stop` and `am start` the relaunched app measured `mean_luminance=219.9` with the same centre, i.e. still light. That is the fix: the mode was held in a `MutableStateFlow` whose own comment said it was 'not persisted: closing the app returns it to following the system', while the slot's specification requires every preference in the surface to survive a restart. It is now written through the same DataStore as the other four preferences. The preference was set back to `Follow the system` and re-measured at `mean_luminance=47.1` with centre `(36,44,36)`, so nothing the owner had set was left changed.

The round's data across the same process death (read on digest 1e61743bfb17), checked rather than assumed. The relaunched app opened on the Round screen reading `Customers 2`, `Total owed $55.00` and `Nobody left today` on the `Due today` tab, so the record, the visits, the corrected payment and the derived balance all came back from disk. $55.00 is the app's own `Balance.balanceFor` - $40.00 mowed for Alice plus $40.00 mowed for Bob minus the $25.00 payment - not a value typed anywhere in the test.

The build behind the record. `node scripts/run-slot-tests.mjs --slot lawn-round-log --rerun` reported `PASS testDebugUnitTest - 35 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped` (32 before this revision added three for the customer-editor fix). `node scripts/verify.mjs --slot lawn-round-log --build` reported `PASS build - assembleDebug` from a single Gradle invocation and 111 PASS rows with no FAIL. `node scripts/prepare-release.mjs --slot lawn-round-log` reported `VERDICT: READY FOR UPLOAD`, the release APK's signature verified by apksigner against the upload certificate, and `python scripts/check-16k.py` on both staged artifacts reported `VERDICT: PASS - every native library is 16 KB ready` (8 libraries, min p_align 0x4000).

The artifact the owner is handed, and that the captured pack actually photographed. The staged release artifact is `dist/lawn-round-log-0.1.0-1-release.apk`, sha256 23aeaae4eb677503a17d92e3a11ead61eaa98b3c010fe52008ed577abe495999. It was installed over the previous release package on this phone, and the installed `/data/app/.../base.apk` hashes to that same value. `store/provenance.json` records that hash in both `artifactSha256` and `installedSha256` with `artifactMatch: exact`, so the six raw captures the pack is composed from were taken from the signed build being uploaded and not from a neighbour of it.

Not a crash, checked rather than assumed: `adb -s R58MB3SGZVL shell logcat -d -b crash` holds no entry for the package across the whole run, including the two handoffs that hand control to a system component.

What the run left on the phone, stated rather than implied. The debug package holds two test customers, a corrected payment and the `DEBUG_UNLOCK` launch; the release package holds the signed build and was force-stopped. The system locale still reads `ru-RU`, the display is still `1080x2340 @ 480`, and no device-wide setting was changed. One file the app did not write is worth naming: `Downloads/lawn-round-log.csv` (358 B, Oct 2) predates this session and is untouched, which is why the Save handoff was cancelled rather than completed. The diagnostics are in `.kiln/scratch/device-fix/` (gitignored and disposable): thirty-eight `uiautomator` dumps, screenshots, and the luminance readings taken from them.
